title: Beyond Kitaev exchange: $Γ'$-driven magnetism in Ag$_3$LiRh$_2$O$_6$
authors: Efrain Insuasti Pazmino, Shi Feng, Ramesh Dhakal, Ioannis Rousochatzakis, Stephen M. Winter, Johannes Knolle, Alexander A. Tsirlin
abstract: In Kitaev magnets, frustration arises from bond-dependent spin anisotropic interactions, which can potentially realize sought-after quantum spin liquid phases. However, material realizations with dominating Kitaev exchange are scarce and the broad parameter space of extended Kitaev models remains largely unexplored experimentally. Here, we use density-functional theory, cluster many-body, spin-wave, and density-matrix renormalization calculations to show that the recently discovered honeycomb rhodate Ag$_3$LiRh$_2$O$_6$ hosts an off-diagonal exchange $Γ_1'$ that is second in magnitude only to the ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange $K_1$. This combination of $K_1$ and $Γ_1'$ explains key experimental observations, an unusually high magnetic ordering temperature of 94 K at ambient pressure and its rapid decrease under hydrostatic pressure as Ag$_3$LiRh$_2$O$_6$ evolves from ferromagnetic toward zigzag order within the honeycomb planes. Our spin-wave calculations further predict an unusual topology of the magnon bands arising from the $Γ_1'$ term in the spin Hamiltonian of the honeycomb layer. We show that the large trigonal splitting of $t_{2g}$ states enhances $Γ_1'$, the hitherto underappreciated term in Kitaev magnets, and opens the way to new interesting regimes of the extended Kitaev model.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the magnetism in $	ext{Ag}_3	ext{LiRh}_2	ext{O}_6$, showing that the off-diagonal $\Gamma'_1$ exchange term is crucial for understanding its high magnetic ordering temperature. By combining DFT, DMRG, and LSWT, the authors map out the phase diagram and predict the magnon band structure, opening new avenues for understanding extended Kitaev physics.
main_problem: To explore magnetism beyond the standard Kitaev exchange model by investigating the role of the $\Gamma'$-driven exchange interaction in the honeycomb rhodate $	ext{Ag}_3	ext{LiRh}_2	ext{O}_6$.
main_result: The combination of the Kitaev exchange ($K_1$) and the off-diagonal $\Gamma'_1$ term successfully explains the material's unusually high magnetic ordering temperature (94 K) and its sensitivity to hydrostatic pressure.
method: The study employs a combination of Density-Functional Theory (DFT), Cluster Many-Body calculations, Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG), and Linear Spin-Wave Theory (LSWT) to analyze the spin Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is the honeycomb rhodate $	ext{Ag}_3	ext{LiRh}_2	ext{O}_6$, modeled by an extended Kitaev Hamiltonian incorporating $K_1$ and $\Gamma'_1$. The analysis compares the ground states of Ferromagnetic (FM) and Zigzag (ZZ) orderings.
key_observables: Magnetic ordering temperature ($T_N$), magnon band topology, and magnetic Bragg peak positions.
important_parameters: Exchange couplings ($ ar{K}_1 \simeq -8.4 	ext{ meV}$, $ ar{\Gamma}'_1 \simeq -4.7 	ext{ meV}$), hydrostatic pressure, and trigonal distortion magnitude.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as mean-field theory, the harmonic approximation in LSWT, and the assumption that the $\Gamma'_1$ term is significant.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the honeycomb plane with exchange couplings, the pressure dependence of $T_N$ shifting the phase between FM and ZZ order, and simulated neutron diffraction patterns for the A-type AFM state.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theoretical framework by first identifying the relevant extended Kitaev model, then using DFT/DMRG to map the phase diagram (FM vs. ZZ) based on exchange parameters, and finally using LSWT to predict the magnon spectrum and magnetic structure factors.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it uses advanced many-body techniques (DMRG, LSWT) to analyze a real material exhibiting complex magnetic behavior, providing a detailed theoretical understanding of how specific lattice distortions enhance previously underestimated exchange terms.

(c) Pressure dependence of the trigonal crystal- field splitting shown in the inset. All solid lines are guides to the eye.

FIG. 2. Pressure evolution of the exchange couplings ob- tained from cluster exact diagonalization (CED) and mean- field estimate of the Ne´el temperature: (a) Leading couplings ¯K1, ¯Γ′ 1 and ¯Γ1. (b) ¯J3 and J⊥constitute the subleading terms, while ¯J1 is rather small and gets even weaker under pressure. (c) Mean-field calculation of TN. At lower pressures, the A- type AFM order reproduces the experimental values, whereas at higher pressures a better agreement is obtained for the zigzag order.

FIG. 3. Phase diagram of the monolayer K1 −Γ1 −Γ′ 1 −J3 model as a function of the normalized interactions −Γ1/|K1| and −Γ′ 1/|K1|, with J3/|K1| = 0.2. Solid and dashed curves mark the DMRG and classical phase boundaries; red and blue dots on the boundaries denote the phase transitions derived from susceptibilities with respect to Γ′ 1 and Γ1; Blue hexago- nal markers in the FM phase show the CED parameters un- der compression. Real-space spin ordering along with static structure factors on the right column are shown for the ferro- magnetic (FM), zigzag, and the double-Q phases respectively.
